Maxon RTD800 Real Tube Overdrive Distortion Pedal Review | GearStrings GEARSTRINGS Home Blog Categories Authors About Home / Blog / gear reviews gear reviews Maxon RTD800 Real Tube Overdrive Distortion Pedal Review By zoe-langford June 13, 2026 Maxon RTD800 Real Tube Overdrive Distortion Pedal Review The Maxon RTD800 Real Tube is a high-fidelity, dual-stage overdrive/distortion pedal that integrates genuine 12AX7 vacuum tubes into its signal path—making it one of only two production pedals (alongside the Fulltone OCD Tube) to do so reliably. It delivers dynamic, touch-sensitive saturation with exceptional harmonic complexity and amp-like compression, but at a premium price and with specific operational constraints. For players prioritizing organic tube behavior over compactness or battery operation—especially those using low-to-medium-gain tube amps or seeking studio-grade distortion textures—the RTD800 justifies its cost. However, it falls short as a gig-ready, battery-powered solution due to its AC-only power requirement and thermal sensitivity. This Maxon RTD800 Real Tube overdrive distortion pedal review evaluates its tonal authenticity, build integrity, practical utility, and suitability across rehearsal, studio, and stage environments. About Maxon RTD800 Real Tube Overdrive Distortion Pedal Review Maxon Electronics Co., Ltd., founded in Tokyo in 1972, pioneered early analog effects including the iconic IOD-10 Ibanez Tube Screamer design (licensed to Ibanez in 1979). Though less visible in mainstream marketing than competitors like Boss or Wampler, Maxon maintains deep engineering credibility—supplying OEM circuits to major brands and retaining strict control over component sourcing and hand-wiring practices. The RTD800 launched in 2021 as part of Maxon’s “Real Tube” series, directly addressing demand for analog tube saturation outside traditional amplifiers. Unlike hybrid designs that use tubes solely for gain staging (e.g., Tech 21 SansAmp), the RTD800 places a single 12AX7 tube in the core signal path after preamp buffering, followed by a discrete Class-A op-amp stage and passive tone network. Its goal isn’t emulation—it’s replication: capturing how tubes behave under voltage swing, thermal drift, and interaction with guitar pickups and amp inputs. First Impressions Unboxing reveals a 165 × 110 × 65 mm (W×D×H) metal chassis with brushed aluminum top panel and matte black powder-coated sides. Weight is 680 g—substantially heavier than most pedals, signaling robust internal construction. The front panel features six controls: Drive (0–10), Tone (0–10), Level (0–10), Mode toggle (OD/DIST), Tube Bias switch (Normal/Hi), and a bright blue LED power indicator. No battery compartment exists; only an IEC C7 socket accepts the included 12 VAC 1.2 A adapter. The tube socket sits flush beneath a removable vented cover secured by two Phillips screws—visible upon removal, but not user-serviceable without soldering tools. Initial setup requires plugging in, waiting ~30 seconds for cathode warm-up (audible soft hum subsides), then adjusting bias per environment: Normal mode suits most home and studio settings; Hi mode increases plate voltage for tighter low-end response and higher headroom, recommended when driving a clean amp channel or pairing with high-output pickups. RTD800                  JAN : 4515615006614 UPC : 840433001775      RTD800 is an overdrive/distortion effect pedal with a real double triode tube. Employs two independent circuits, one each for overdrive and distortion. Wide range of tube sound from traditional overdrive to metallic distortion can be easily created. Boost circuit boosts output level by approx. 5dB. (factory default setting) Boost level is variable (3dB to 9dB). With BOOST switch, solos and rhythms can be instantly changed. BOOST LED lights when BOOST switch is on. Your favorite tone can be created with just 3 controls. Employs NR with high-performance VCA (voltage controlled amplifier) to cut harsh noise. Variable threshold level makes your own setting easier. NR ON/OFF is selectable. Employs NR status LED for easily viewable setting. The LED lights when noise decreases. NR status can be checked with the LED during performance. 9VDC supplied from AC adaptor is bumped up to 12.6V and stabilized by a DC to DC voltage converter and then supplied to each circuit. When power is turned on, tube heater inrush current control circuit extends tube life. TBS (True Bypass Switching) using 4PDT mechanical switch. AC adaptor AC2009 can be used worldwide from 100VAC to 240VAC by auto voltage sensing. Main countries’ safety standard approved. FCC Part 15 compliant. RoHS compliant. Made in Japan with confidence.
